Tunnel disabled manually. The “%1$s” rule would have turned it on: your choice is respected, and the rules will take over at the next network change.
Tunnel enabled manually. The “%1$s” rule would have turned it off: your choice is remembered and will be replayed on this network. Manage the preference from the Networks screen.
Tunnel disabled manually. The “%1$s” rule would have turned it on: your choice is remembered and will be replayed on this network. Manage the preference from the Networks screen.

Tailscale Auto Rules turns your Tailscale tunnel on or off depending on the network: off on your trusted Wi-Fi, on everywhere else — mobile data included. Once set up, the app never asks for anything again.\n\nIt drives the official Tailscale app, which must be installed: it replaces neither the client nor the VPN.

Watching the network continuously requires a visible service: Android imposes a permanent notification on it. It is not a setting — it shows the live tunnel state and the rule that decided it, and lets you turn off automation without opening the app.

Android restricts reading Wi-Fi network names (SSID) to apps allowed to access location. Without it, your trusted networks cannot be recognised.\n\nOnly the network name is read: neither your position nor your movements are read, stored or transmitted.

When you turn Tailscale on or off by hand on a network, the app can remember that choice and replay it every time you return to that network. Learned preferences are managed from the Networks screen, and this setting can be changed at any time in Settings.
Automation is off: the tunnel will no longer change on its own. Turn it back on from Settings.
Install the official Tailscale app: without it, no rule can be applied.
Automatically turns the tunnel on when on mobile data (4G/5G).

Force the tunnel network by network — off on your trusted networks, on where you require it. Networks not in the list follow the automation, and your gestures in Tailscale are recorded here too. Swipe a card sideways to hand the network back to the automation.
No preference: the automation decides everywhere — tunnel off nowhere, on across every network.
This network is already in the list.
The network name cannot be empty.

Android restricts reading Wi-Fi network names to apps allowed to access location. Without it, your trusted networks cannot be recognised. This app only looks at the network name: neither your position nor your movements are read, stored or transmitted.

Remembers when you turn the tunnel on or off by hand, network by network, and replays it. Preferences already learned keep applying until you delete them.
